questions.prompt: Which value is the untrusted source in the hotel search?

options.text: The `city` query-string parameter of GET /api/hotels
The `listingStatus` column stored in SQLite
The participant alias generated at registration

In `app/src/server.js`, when the route reads `req.query`

options.text: `console.log` in the server startup handler
`res.json` returning the hotels array
`db.prepare(query.sql)` executing the composed statement

questions.prompt: Which file builds the statement that reaches that sink?

options.text: `app/src/search-query.js`
`app/src/workshop-progress.js`
`app/src/board-client.js`

questions.prompt: What makes the data flow unsafe?

options.text: The result set is serialized to JSON

questions.prompt: Why does `normalizeSearchTerm` fail to stop the attack?

options.text: It runs after the SQL statement is prepared

questions.prompt: Which business boundary does the payload break?

options.text: Only listings with `listingStatus = 'PUBLIC'` may be returned

A search must return at most ten results

questions.prompt: What is the runtime evidence that the boundary broke?

options.text: The application returned HTTP 500
A normal Paris search returned two listings

questions.prompt: Which correction addresses the root cause?

options.text: Blocking requests that contain `OR 1=1`
Binding the city value as a query parameter
